content.key_idea: A single decision tree, split into four subsystem lanes, cascades Z-score threshold checks so the metrics closest to the root are the ones most sensitive to a faulty machine.
content.reading_order: Top-down through the dashed boundary: each blue Z-score box is read before branching right to an orange Abnormal leaf or continuing down.

style.stroke: thin (~0.83pt), rounded corners; solid curved arrows for edges, dashed for the lane separators and outer boundary
style.arrows: curved connecting lines from each check down to the next check and across to Abnormal, each labelled low/high

encoding.color_means: blue = a Z-score threshold check to evaluate; orange = the Abnormal (faulty) verdict reached when that check exceeds threshold
encoding.line_style_means: solid curved arrows connect each check to its low/high outcomes; dashed lines separate the four subsystem lanes and outline the overall boundary
encoding.state_means: checks are told apart only by fill colour (blue = check, orange = Abnormal verdict), not by position alone
encoding.marker_means: 'low'/'high' edge labels mark which branch a threshold comparison follows
encoding.emphasis: the orange Abnormal boxes stand out against the uniform blue checks, drawing attention to how quickly a fault gets flagged
reusable_patterns: repeated check-node cascade (low: next check, high: verdict leaf), grouped into lanes by subsystem
weaknesses: the final check's 'low' branch has no explicit 'Normal' leaf drawn, leaving the non-faulty outcome implicit

evidence: Minder uses a decision tree to prioritize the sensitivity of each metric in identifying the faulty machine
PFC, CPU, GPU, and NVLink-related metrics are identified as the most informative ones
Nodes located closer to the root of the tree indicate that the corresponding monitoring metrics are more sensitive

summary: Figure 7 shows the top seven layers of Minder's decision tree for prioritizing which monitoring metric to check when a training machine is suspected faulty. Enclosed in a single dashed boundary and split into four horizontal lanes by subsystem (Inter-host network/PFC, Central processing/CPU, Computation/GPU, Intra-host network/NVLink), the tree cascades through Z-score checks in fixed order: PFC Tx Packet Rate, CPU Usage, GPU Duty Cycle, GPU Power Draw, GPU Graphics Engine Activity, GPU Tensor Activity, and NVLink Bandwidth. At every blue check node, a 'high' branch peels off to an orange terminal 'Abnormal' box, while 'low' continues down to the next, more specific check, so nodes nearer the root are the metrics most sensitive to a fault.
summary_zh: 图7为Minder决策树前7层：按PFC、CPU、GPU、NVLink四个子系统分层，逐层检测指标Z-score，判高则分到橙色Abnormal，判低则进入下一层，越靠根部的指标对故障越敏感。
